newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Former Russian deputy minister heads IFCI bank.
newsitem.headline: Former Russian deputy minister heads IFCI bank.

text.p: Former First Deputy Finance Minister Andrei Vavilov, who was in charge of Russia's Eurobond programme, has joined one of its biggest banks, AKB Mezhdunarodnaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (MFK) as president, a bank spokesman said on Friday.
"The reason for the appointment was his high professional qualities and a huge experience of analysing the situation in Russia and on the world financial markets," the spokesman said.
Vavilov became MFK president on May 15.
He had been First Deputy Finance Minister since 1992. He was in charge of the hard currency department, and chaired an intergovernment commission on foreign debt and assets.
MFK has been without a president since the middle of 1996 when its former head Alexander Khloponin became chief executive of Norilsk Nickel.
